## What code will check of you (continued from handoff-keys.md)

`<T>` is your ticket, `<ID>` your dispatch id, `<home>` the project's qa-factory folder - all three stand in your prompt (`Ticket: ... Dispatch: ...`) and in your task packet.

- [execution_request:place_rows] Every test file the manifest names for an asked case exists under the run directory or the project root (a path relative to the project root). Door: correct `file` through `manifest_put.py` (path relative to the project root), or pass `--cwd` when the test lives in a sandbox.
- [execution_request:profile] The execution profile of the run is known without a guess: a profile named by `--profile` or a manifest row's `profile_id` is one `qa-factory/config.json` holds; the asked cases run under one profile; a row that names no profile and whose file lies under another profile's test root, or a root several profiles share, names its `profile_id`; when nothing else tells, `--profile` names it. Door: `profile_id` on the manifest row through `manifest_put.py --fragment`, or `--profile ID` (only where the caller takes it: `run_suite --mine`, never `probe_by_code`); cases of two profiles: one `--mine` per profile.
- [execution_request:purpose] `purpose` is one of `PURPOSES` and never `impact_regression`. Door: `run_suite.py --template request`, or `run_suite.py --mine <CASE>`.
- [execution_request:runtime] `runtime_provenance` is present, its `profile_id` matches the selected profile and it is matched or person_confirmed; a runtime-required request carries a read-only `runtime_probe` with a non-empty argv, an existing cwd and a positive timeout. Door: `run_suite.py --template request`, or `run_suite.py --mine <CASE>`.
- [execution_request:selection] `selected_instance_ids` and `current_scope_instance_ids` are string arrays, every selected instance is in the approved current scope, a behavioural request selects at least one, and only supported selectors are used. Door: `run_suite.py --template request`, or `run_suite.py --mine <CASE>`.
- [execution_request:selector] A behavioural command has a verified adapter selector contract and framework `selector_args`: non-empty string arrays, never holding `{report_path}`. Door: `run_suite.py --template request`, or `run_suite.py --mine <CASE>`.
- [execution_request:selector_args] A manifest row of a profile that does not run pytest carries `selector_args` (the framework's own arguments) and `report_test_id`, unless the factory can build the selection from a `run_forms` direct form. Door: give the row `selector_args` and `report_test_id` through `manifest_put.py` once; until then run through `--template request`.
- [execution_request:stand] The stand the run would stand on can be looked at now, and it runs this story's build. Door: name it as `environment` in your digest (`stand_health.py --probe --env <environment>`); a stand that runs another build: the person's word at the build question of the stage entry.
- [execution_request:stand.reference] The story's record does not name its own stand (`pipeline.json` `environment`) as the reference (old version) of a side as well. Door: tell the conductor in your digest which stand runs the new version (the record is corrected by `stage_done.py --set sides.<side>.reference=...`, a conductor command - F-W2).
- [execution_request:window_first] A run that picks part of a case (`--node-id`) does not leave tests of the same file in the dispatch's scope that have never run in this window: one call runs them together. Door: run the command the answer names (`run_suite.py --mine <cases>`); only what a repair touched: `--purpose repair_verify`; this exact run once more: `--again`.
- [manifest_put:assertion_line] Every `assertion_id` `<file>:<line>` stands on a line that holds a check (`probe_by_code.check_on_line`). Door: point the id at the assertion's line.
- [manifest_put:base_outcome] `base_outcome` is `{"outcome": refused|working, "run": <non-empty run id>}`. Door: run the same command again with the fixed value.
- [manifest_put:colliding_ids] Two rows of one fragment that resolve to one instance id never name different test files. Door: rename one function or split the fragment, then `manifest_put.py` again.
- [manifest_put:ghost_rows] A fragment never binds a Then to an id it retracts in the same fragment, and never sends a ghost row of an instance the manifest retracted. Door: drop the row or the retract.
- [manifest_put:helper_rows] An `introduced_helpers[]` row has `file`, `name` and the four role fields as strings, `novelty` (new, changed or unknown) only when the writer sent it, and no other key. Door: run the same command again with the fixed row.
- [manifest_put:novelty] A `tests[]` row carries `novelty` only as the whole row form `manifest_from_tests.py` writes (an object with `measured_on` and `measured_by`, no `resolved`). Door: leave `novelty` out; code writes it.
- [manifest_put:obligation_hash] A row never sends an `obligation_hash` the code did not build (`content_hash(obligation_refs)`). Door: leave it out; code writes it.
- [manifest_put:provisional] `provisional` is a list of rows in the registry's provisional form. Door: run the same command again with the fixed row.
- [manifest_put:retract] `retract` never names `tests`, `unresolved` or `obligation_bindings` (never replaced whole) and is otherwise well formed. Door: change those keys row by row.
- [manifest_put:revision] `expected_revision` equals the revision the manifest file shows now. Door: read the file's revision and send again.
- [manifest_put:then_remainder] A Then-level hand-off row has the contract's Then-remainder form (a case with a whole-case `unresolved[]` row keeps its echo rows). Door: run the same command again with the fixed row.
- [manifest_put:unknown_obligation] `obligation_bindings[]` name only obligations the plan names, in the plan's own spelling. Door: copy the obligation ids from the plan.
- [run_suite:begin] A request's `idempotency_key` is new, or names the very request (same digest) already recorded under it; a key another process is claiming at the same moment is not reused. Door: write the request with a new `idempotency_key` (a `--mine` run takes a key of its own: run it again); a claim that cannot be read: `--recover <key> --task <T>`.
- [s5_precheck:bindings] Every Then clause of every case in scope is bound to a test and an assertion (`then_bindings`), or is a remainder the person took (`then handed:`), named. Door: bind the clause, or name the remainder.
- [s5_precheck:environment] A `blocked_by_env` row of this dispatch carries the fix it found (`remedy`), names no credential value, blames the stand for no fixture the approved case never asked for, and stands on a run that shows the stand. Door: each finding's `fix`.
- [s5_precheck:manifest] The manifest of this dispatch's cases keeps the invariants `manifest_put.py` owns (one instance per id, a covering row per scoped case), as a hand edit would break them. Door: each finding's `fix`.
- [s5_precheck:obligations] Every coverage obligation of the plan row a scoped case belongs to has an `obligation_bindings[]` row, under the plan's own id, reaching that case. Door: add the binding through `manifest_put.py`.
- [s5_precheck:oracle] A test never asserts an expected value the case left `open` or `invalid`; a test that went red and later passed on changed code has an `expectation_changes[]` record whose `then_refs` resolve; an unresolved row never disputes the approved case. Door: each finding's `fix`.
- [s5_precheck:row_fields] `assertion_id`: the assertion that fails when the behaviour breaks (a file:line or an id); `defect_location`: the product location the obligation damages (a file:line); `change_disposition`: `new_or_changed` or `unchanged`; `change_basis_ref`: what the disposition is read from (for example `manifest:<case>`); `obligation_refs`: the plan's obligation ids the test proves, as [{"obligation_id": "<plan obligation id>"}]; the code adds each hash; `profile_id`: the execution profile that runs the test; the file lies under a test root several profiles share. Door: add the named field to the row through `manifest_put.py`.
- [s5_precheck:run_mapping] Every test of the scope has a reporter row in its run block. Door: `run_suite.py --reparse-block`, never a rerun.
- [validate_artifacts:check_manifest_invariants] No two `tests[]` entries carry one instance id, no case is green in `tests[]` and present in `unresolved[]`, and no `self_fixes[]` entry repeats an earlier one byte for byte. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_manifest_v0] Every `automate` case of the plan has a `tests[]` or `unresolved[]` row; a `tests[]` row names an existing file and a `marker` or a full content-bound trace; an `unresolved` reason is from its list; a critic verdict is from its list, with `fix_notes[]` only for `approved_with_fixes`. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_marker_in_file] The marker a manifest row names stands in the test file it names. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_remedy_rows] A row blocked on the environment carries a `remedy` that is the fix, and names no value of a credential key. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [validate_artifacts:check_self_fixes] A `self_fixes[]` entry carries every required key and never drops a Then line's assertion that was there before. Door: edit the file and the field the refusal line names.
- [guard_pre_tool:*] 24 checks of your tool calls are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door; nothing you have written is lost by them.
- [stage_guard:*] 7 checks of your tool calls are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door; nothing you have written is lost by them.
- [host_adapter:*] 6 checks of your tool calls are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door; nothing you have written is lost by them.
- [execution_request:*] 5 checks of your test-run calls (`run_suite.py`, `red_sandbox.py`, `probe_by_code.py`) are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door; a refused call launches no test. Write a request file from `run_suite.py --template request`, never from memory.
- [run_suite:*] 5 checks of your commands are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door.
- [role_cli:*] 3 checks of your commands are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door. Run `case_versions.py --help`, `execution_fingerprint.py --help`, `manifest_put.py --help` before you write an input file: it prints what each command of the script checks.

### Only in a plan dispatch (replaces "Only in a window")

- [controller:s5_plan_accept] A plan dispatch never closes S5: it is accepted without `stage_complete` (no `--complete`). Door: finish the plan dispatch without `--complete`.
- [controller:s5_plan_gaps] Your plan has no gap the plan check names (the refusal lists up to six). Door: repair the named rows of `work/s5-plan.json`.
- [exit_gate:EG-s5-plan-outputs] Before you end an S5 dispatch, every output the S5 plan names for your role is written. Door: write the output the refusal names before you end the dispatch.

### Only in a window (replaced by "Only in a plan dispatch")

- [manifest_put:expectation_changes] An expectation change names its function(s), red_attempt, green_attempt (or null), then_refs as `[{case, then: int}]`, what_changed, and a reason for a new row; the patch verdict joins; critic_verdict is a list, critic_note a string, and a note stands for each NOTE_REQUIRED_VERDICTS verdict. Door: fix the entry the refusal names.
